title: Connection order in `.tscn` file unpredictable and unstable
body:
### Tested versions

- v4.7-beta2
- v4.6.2-stable

### System information

Godot v4.7.beta2 - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 3 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon RX 6700 XT (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.21030.2001) - AMD Ryzen 7 5800X3D 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 31.91 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

Signal order is unstable and unpredictable in the `.tscn` file, when the source and destination are the same (but methods differ).

For example:

```
[connection signal="hidden" from="." to="Button1" method="sig_result_6a"]
[connection signal="hidden" from="." to="Button1" method="sig_result_5a"]
[connection signal="hidden" from="." to="Button1" method="sig_result_4a"]
[connection signal="hidden" from="." to="Button1" method="sig_result_3a"]
[connection signal="hidden" from="." to="Button1" method="sig_result_2a"]
[connection signal="hidden" from="." to="Button1" method="sig_result_1a"]
```

Could also be:

```
[connection signal="hidden" from="." to="Button1" method="sig_result_6a"]
[connection signal="hidden" from="." to="Button1" method="sig_result_5a"]
[connection signal="hidden" from="." to="Button1" method="sig_result_2a"]
[connection signal="hidden" from="." to="Button1" method="sig_result_4a"]
[connection signal="hidden" from="." to="Button1" method="sig_result_3a"]
[connection signal="hidden" from="." to="Button1" method="sig_result_1a"]
```

In the same exact configuration, it will be stable. Things that I've tested that cause a new order:

- A project upgrade (4.6.2-stable to 4.7-beta2)
- Changing the script file the methods appear in (adding method body, etc)
- Reordering methods in a script file

This makes it annoying for version control systems to not have bogus changes appear to a bunch of files when one of these things change.

I hypothesize what's happening is that each Callable is assigned an object ID, and whenever that object ID might change, signal order is randomized. 

This also makes it impossible for third-party `.tscn` file deserializers and serializers to mimic Godot's behavior, because the order cannot be inferred simply from the `.tscn` contents. Not good!

**The fix:** We should lexically sort the `.tscn` connection entries. If the order indeed doesn't matter, we'd better sort them stably, in a way that doesn't rely on secret information external to the `.tscn` file. Because connections are automatically deduped, we can just order by `(from, to, signal, method)` in that order. I would highly recommend using the UUID from `from` and `to`, rather than the path. That way, when reordering nodes, the connection order doesn't change either.

### Steps to reproduce

- Open the MRP
- Check out `stupid_signals.tscn` 
- Observe that the order is impossible to predict
- Do something to mess with the Callable IDs (I think?):
    - Change Godot version
    - Mess with `stupid_signals.gd`; it's reliable to add an empty new method to the top and bottom of the file.
    - Delete .godot and %appdata%/app_userdata
- Reopen the editor
- Move something in `stupid_signals.tscn` and save
- Observe that the order has (probably) changed

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[signal-hell.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27937189/signal-hell.zip)
